topSignals.title: Quiet day continues — Elcogen now 53 days quiet, Topsoe 78 days; no genuinely new item found in any monitored section today.
topSignals.text: Dedicated English- and German-language searches for both priority stacks, the Tier 2 dedicated rotation (Kyocera, Aisin — round 3) and sweep, the Tier 3 dedicated rotation (cycle 9, round 3: Fraunhofer IKTS/Kerafol, Plansee, Huatsing Power, Ningbo SOFCMAN, Chaozhou Three-Circle/CCTC, Watt Fuel Cell) and two further Tier 3 sweeps, and broad AI-datacenter/hyperscaler, regulation, competing-power, market/financials, research/IP, and scientific-paper checks all returned only recycled/already-logged background or out-of-window items. The "Renewable Innovations" DOE fuel-cell/AI-datacenter item flagged on Nov 10-12 is now resolved: Renewable Innovations is confirmed (via its FCHEA profile and military mobile-power-generator coverage) to build PEM hydrogen fuel cells using GM's Gen2 HYDROTEC stacks, not solid oxide — it is closed out as non-SOFC and removed from the watch list. items.text: Elcogen (priority): No new news-archive item since Sept 21, 2026 (Metrosert cooperation), confirmed via English- and German-language searches today — 53 days quiet. Status unchanged: elcoStack E3000 G2 platform (75% FC electrical efficiency / 90% with heat recovery, 33 kWh/kg H2 SOEC — vendor claims) in volume production at the 360 MW/yr ELCO I Tallinn factory.

Topsoe (priority): No new solid-oxide-specific release since the Aug 27, 2026 H1 2026 results/SOEC pathway reset, confirmed via English- and German-language searches today — 78 days quiet; topsoe.com/press-releases remains dominated by PTX/ammonia/SAF/blue-hydrogen news (most recently a DKK 4.4bn PTX restructuring item), out of SOFC/SOEC scope.

Today's Tier 2 dedicated rotation (Kyocera, Aisin — round 3): no new item for either; both companies' top headlines remain legacy background (Kyocera's 3 kW institutional-cogeneration SOFC and ceramics/ECD product pages; Aisin's 2025-vintage hydrogen/fuel-cell strategy writeups).

Today's Tier 2 sweep — "Bloom Energy OR FuelCell Energy OR Ceres Power OR Sunfire OR SolydEra": no new item; results repeated already-logged Bloom/NTT DATA and FuelCell Energy/StabilityMax background recirculated by aggregator sites (enkiai.com, Latitude Media).

Today's Tier 3 dedicated rotation — cycle 9, round 3 (Fraunhofer IKTS/Kerafol, Plansee, Huatsing Power, Ningbo SOFCMAN, Chaozhou Three-Circle/CCTC, Watt Fuel Cell): no new items for any of the six; results repeated Fraunhofer IKTS's standing electrolysis-platform/annual-report background, Plansee's legacy conference-paper presence, Huatsing's recirculating Chinese SOFC-sector-research notes (Founder/Guosen Securities), Ningbo SOFCMAN's absence from current search results beyond a generic manufacturer listing, Chaozhou Three-Circle's routine HKEX/earnings filings (H-share listing process, Q3 2026 results), and Watt Fuel Cell's standing WATT HOME residential-SOFC rollout and equity-financing news (all pre-dated).
Tier 3 sweep — "Reverion OR Convion OR Hexis OR Doosan Fuel Cell OR SK ecoplant": no new item; recycled the standing Doosan-Reverion $76.7-78M SOFC stack-supply background.

Tier 3 sweep — "OxEon Energy OR Nexceris OR Kawasaki Heavy Industries OR Miura OR Weichai": no new item; recycled the Miura/Ceres 4.2kW launch and Weichai/Ceres manufacturing-licence/CE-certification background.
Competitor roster: SOFC systems for data centers

Bloom Energy: Deployed/signed at multiple named sites — Oracle/Project Jupiter, AEP (1 GW), Brookfield EaaS, Nebius (328 MW/$2.6B), Equinix (>100 MW/19 sites), Aligned "Project Phoenix" (2 GW), Hitachi (Japan), SK Eternix (28 MW, operational), NTT DATA (900 MW, global, shipments from 2027).

FuelCell Energy (incl. HyAxiom-branded products): Signed orders/PPAs — Fit Energy (up to 380 MW), Inuverse Korea (up to 100 MW), Texas CRA (75 MW), SDCL (up to 450 MW). Also hosting a DOE/national-lab-backed R&D testbed (StabilityMax) in Danbury, CT. No named commercial deployment live yet.
Doosan Fuel Cell/HyAxiom: Signed order — US AI data center supply contract (KRW 823.6B); supplies SOFC stacks to Reverion. No named data-center site of its own yet.
Convion: Pipeline-only/pre-commercial under HD Hyundai ownership; no named data-center customer.
SK ecoplant: Pipeline-only; no new named data-center deployment.
Ceres Power's SOFC licensees (Doosan, Delta Electronics, Weichai): Licensing/pipeline-only; no named data-center deployment via Ceres licensing directly.
Reverion: Pipeline-only — Doosan-supplied SOFC stacks for rSOC power plants (Germany); no named data-center customer yet.
Petra Power: Pre-commercial, no named customer; first infrastructure deployment targeted 2028.
